- #10807 (filed 12:07Z, two minutes after this card) diagnosed the same three failing cases to the mechanism your hypothesis section suspected: git approxidate resolves a bare `--since=YYYY-MM-DD` at the **current wall-clock time**, so the fixture's 12:00:00Z commit stamps fall out of the window every day after 12:00 UTC. Deterministic red-for-twelve-hours, green-for-twelve.
- Fix landed in **PR #10811** (merged; gives the self-test windows a complete instant instead of an approxidated bare date). #10807 closed 12:41Z.
- **Re-verified on current `origin/main` = `5f2e54c` at ~13:05Z — i.e. inside the after-noon half of the day that used to fail**: `node scripts/pm/git-history.mjs --self-test` → `all cases passed`, `EXIT=0`, on a fresh detached worktree.

Blast-radius note for the lanes watching #10766 / #10800 / #10739: the failure was main's, so those PRs need only a re-run of `Lint & Repo Gates` (or their next push) to clear — no diff change required.

Your second executable criterion ("the self-test must not be able to rot silently with the calendar") is carried by #10814 (open, devx finding pool: the three shallow-history self-tests run under `bash -e`, first failure masks the rest) and by #10807's closing evidence, which required proof on both sides of 12:00 UTC.
